entry.name: jit.textfile
entry.digest: Read and write a matrix as an ASCII text file
entry.description: The jit.textfile object maintains a text buffer, into which a text file or char matrix can be imported. The buffer can also be edited directly by double-clicking on the object to open an editor window. A bang to the object causes the text buffer to be sent out the left outlet as a matrix.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.digest: Double-click to open an editor window
messages.description: Double-clicking on the object opens a text editor window with the current contents of the text buffer.

messages.name: line
messages.digest: Output a line as a string matrix
messages.description: Sends the line specified by the argument out the middle outlet of the object as a string matrix (1 dimensional char matrix, 0 terminated) that can be used by theset of objects. Line numbering starts at 1.

messages.name: open
messages.description: Opens the text editor window. Sending this message is equivalent to double-clicking on the object.

messages.name: outputline
messages.digest: Sends the matrix out the middle outlet
messages.description: Sends the matrix out the middle outlet. This is equivalent to themessage, but uses to the middle outlet rather than the left outlet. (For this object, themessage refers only to the left outlet).

messages.name: read
messages.description: Reads a text file from disk if a filename is specified. Otherwise, an file dialog box will appear so that a text file can be specified.

messages.name: wclose
messages.description: Closes the editor window, if open.

messages.name: write
messages.digest: Write the text buffer to a disk file
messages.description: Writes the object's text buffer to a disk file. The optional argument specifies a file name.
